title: Synchronized free-breathing CT
text: Daniel Low and colleagues at Washington University in St. Louis reconstruct four-dimensional CT scans synchronized to a breathing signal measured during free breathing.

title: The breathing motion model
text: Tissue position is written as a function of tidal volume and airflow, the model that gives 5DCT its name.

title: Characterizing the model
text: Free-breathing patterns described with the 5D model, followed by the continuity equation in 2010 and a biomechanical interpretation of the model parameters in 2011.

title: The lab moves to UCLA
text: Daniel Low joins the UCLA Department of Radiation Oncology as Vice Chair of Medical Physics.

title: Fast-helical acquisition
text: A new acquisition and analysis technique replaces slow ciné scanning with repeated fast helical free-breathing scans, the protocol in use today.

title: Accuracy and comparison
text: A ground-truth accuracy method for 5DCT, and the first comparison of breathing-gated 5DCT images against a commercial 4DCT protocol.

title: Preparing for clinical use
text: Prospective gating to diversify the scan set, the model's dependence on breathing rate, minimum scan parameters, and a comparison of tumor motion measurements against the commercial protocol.

title: Routine clinical use
text: 5DCT enters routine use for thoracic treatment planning at UCLA in March 2019, supported by safety-oriented in-house software. The McSART motion-compensated cone-beam CT algorithm is published the same year.

title: Ventilation
text: Regional ventilation measured directly from the 25 fast-helical scans.

title: Applications of free-breathing CT
text: Michael Lauria completes a Ph.D. applying fast-helical free-breathing CT to cone-beam reconstruction, ventilation, airway modeling, and elasticity.

title: A benchmark for 4DCT 2.0
text: An editorial in the Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics on the future of 4DCT names 5DCT, from Daniel Low and colleagues, as the benchmark for what it calls 4DCT 2.0.

title: Motion-compensated cone-beam CT
text: Patient-specific 5DCT motion models applied to cone-beam CT reconstruction in a pilot study. Michael Lauria joins the faculty.

title: Review of the first clinical workflow
text: A retrospective analysis of the first clinical 5DCT workflow, and a review of thoracic image registration and respiratory motion management with the group's clinical collaborators.

title: Recognition
text: Claudia Miller completes a Ph.D. on the clinical 5DCT workflow. Daniel Low receives the ASTRO Gold Medal.
